hero.headline: Oil Prices Jump 6% as U.S. and Iran Exchange Military Strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices climbed sharply following a new round of military exchanges between the United States and Iran, with the main international oil benchmark rising 6 percent. Energy markets remain sensitive to any disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes.

According to U.S. officials, American forces carried out strikes targeting an Iranian military facility and successfully shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz. A ground control station in Iran's Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone was also hit. U.S. Central Command described the actions as "measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire."

Iran responded approximately two hours later. Iranian state media reported that the Revolutionary Guards had targeted an American military base in Kuwait in retaliation. Kuwait's army confirmed that its air defense systems were intercepting hostile missile and drone threats early Thursday morning.

The escalation coincided with reports that Iranian forces fired on four commercial vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media said the incident occurred without prior coordination with security forces but provided no details on the ships or any damage.

The fresh military strikes underscored widening divisions between Washington and Tehran in negotiations aimed at resolving their broader conflict. President Donald Trump warned that if Iran did not reach an acceptable deal, "we'll have to just finish the job." He claimed Iran was "negotiating on fumes" and stated that the administration would not be pressured by upcoming elections to rush into an agreement.

One unresolved disagreement centers on whether a U.S.-Iran ceasefire would extend to Israel's operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran has insisted that any ceasefire agreement must cover Lebanese operations, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said his military is "deepening its operation" in Lebanon. Israeli forces have struck over 550 targets this week and have clashed with Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon's strategic areas.

The humanitarian toll continues mounting. More than 1.2 million Lebanese have been displaced since March, and Israeli strikes have killed over 3,200 people according to Lebanon's health ministry. Fighting has persisted despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire announced in April, which now appears close to collapse.

Analysts warned that current oil price increases could represent just the beginning if shipping disruptions persist. The Strait of Hormuz closure would force tankers to take longer routes around Africa, adding significant costs and delays to global oil deliveries. With limited spare production capacity and inventories, traders are closely monitoring both military developments and diplomatic channels for signs of whether the conflict will expand or stabilize.

cards.headline: Multiple people killed in Oregon shooting, officer hospitalized
cards.body:
Three people were killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego in California, with authorities investigating the incident as a hate crime. Two suspects, aged 17 and 18, died from apparent self-inflicted gunshot wounds.

The shooting occurred shortly before midday prayer at the Islamic Center, located in the Clairemont area of San Diego and the largest mosque in San Diego County. Police had been searching for the two teens after the mother of one suspect called authorities approximately two hours before the attack, reporting that her son was missing along with several of her weapons and her vehicle.

When officers received a 911 call from the Islamic Center, nearby police rushed to the scene and found three people had been shot dead. Dispatchers simultaneously received another report of someone shooting from a vehicle two blocks away. A landscaper was struck but may have been saved when the bullet deflected off his helmet, according to San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl.

Among those killed was a security guard at the center, identified by a family friend as Amin Abdullah. Wahl said the guard's actions were heroic and undoubtedly saved lives, though investigators were still confirming details of exactly what occurred. "He wanted to defend the innocent so he decided to become a security guard," said Shaykh Uthman Ibn Farooq, who had spoken with Abdullah's son.

Authorities confirmed that no children at the center's school were harmed, and a reunification center was established for affected families. The FBI indicated it was investigating the shooting and established a tip line seeking public information.

Police have not released the names of the other two victims. No specific threat had been made against the Islamic Center, but investigators recovered evidence that the attackers engaged in what Wahl described as "generalized hate rhetoric." The FBI confirmed there were no officers involved in firing their weapons.

San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said at a press conference: "Hate has no home in San Diego. Islamophobia has no home in San Diego. An attack on any San Diegan is an attack on all San Diegans."

Taha Hassane, an imam and director of the center, said the community was mourning. "Worshippers anywhere should not have to fear for their lives while attending prayers," said Tazheen Nizam, executive director of the Council on American-Islamic Relations, which condemned the shooting.

California Governor Gavin Newsom said he had been briefed on the situation and offered condolences to affected families and communities. In response to the shooting, law enforcement agencies in Los Angeles and New York announced increased patrols at mosques and other places of worship out of an abundance of caution.

cards.headline: Iran suspends talks with US over Israeli strikes in Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iran halted negotiations with the United States and threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz after Israeli attacks in Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran has suspended talks with the United States, citing Israeli military operations in Lebanon and Gaza as the reason. The move comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered strikes on southern Beirut suburbs in response to Hezbollah rocket and drone attacks on northern Israel.

Despite Iran's announcement of suspended talks, Trump stated that negotiations with Iran were continuing at a rapid pace. The development threatens recent diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Hezbollah signals readiness for full ceasefire with Israel
cards.teaser: A Lebanese official informed the United States that Hezbollah is prepared to accept a full ceasefire with Israel under a US proposal.
cards.body:
Lebanon's embassy in the United States communicated that Hezbollah has agreed to a reciprocal ceasefire with Israel under terms proposed by the US government. The development represents a potential breakthrough in efforts to halt escalating violence between the militant group and Israel.

Trump claimed that both Netanyahu and Hezbollah had agreed to reduce hostilities. The White House has been conducting calls with Israeli officials and representatives connected to Hezbollah amid hopes that a ceasefire arrangement can take hold and prevent further deterioration of security in the region.

cards.headline: Doctors criticize Trump vaccine policy modeled after Denmark
cards.teaser: Medical professionals objected after the president doubled down on a vaccine approach based on Danish practices.
cards.body:
Doctors have criticized President Trump for defending a vaccine policy that he said was modeled after Denmark's approach. The medical community's objections came after Trump doubled down on the policy direction. Danish researchers themselves expressed surprise at the comparison, calling the U.S. adoption of their model bizarre.

The pushback from both American physicians and Danish researchers suggests the Trump administration may have misinterpreted or misapplied aspects of Denmark's vaccine policies. The specific details of the policy and how it differs from current U.S. practice were not elaborated in available reporting, though the negative reaction from medical experts indicates significant professional concerns about the approach.

cards.headline: Trump administration scraps $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund after Republican pushback
cards.teaser: The Trump administration abandoned its nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund following criticism from congressional Republicans and a court challenge ques.
cards.body:
The Trump administration abandoned a $1.8 billion fund created from an IRS settlement after facing opposition from Republican lawmakers and a legal challenge. Republican Representative Kat Cammack criticized the fund as a "billion-dollar-plus slush fund," arguing it wasn't an appropriate solution to government weaponization concerns. The administration dismantled the fund later that same day.

The fund drew immediate scrutiny from within Trump's own party, with more than a dozen Republican senators urging the administration to reverse course. Critics characterized it as a scheme favoring political allies while lacking transparency and oversight. A federal judge in Florida reopened the underlying IRS case, adding legal pressure to the controversial initiative.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes off Massachusetts coast with force of 300 tons of TNT
cards.teaser: A meteor detonated over Cape Cod Bay, creating a sonic boom that shook homes across New England.
cards.body:
A meteor roughly 3 feet wide exploded over the New Hampshire-Massachusetts border north of Boston, releasing energy equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The event generated loud booms that were heard across a wide area, from New England into Canada, with reports reaching as far south as Delaware.

Residents throughout the region reported hearing the explosion and some witnessed the fireball streaking across the sky. NASA confirmed the event occurred over the weekend.

cards.headline: Justice Department to abide by court pause on anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: The Justice Department will comply with a court order temporarily halting its $1.776 billion fund for victims of government weaponization.
cards.body:
The Justice Department said it will comply with a court order temporarily halting a $1.8 billion fund created to compensate victims of alleged government "weaponization." The department stated it strongly disagreed with the court's decision but would follow the ruling.

The fund stemmed from a settlement in a case involving the Trump administration and the Internal Revenue Service. The initiative drew unusual criticism from Republican senators and faced widespread public opposition, prompting the Trump administration to retreat from the program.

cards.headline: Iran suspends talks with US over Israeli strikes in Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iran halted negotiations with the United States and threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz after Israeli attacks in Lebanon.

Despite Iran's announcement of suspended talks, Trump stated that negotiations with Iran were continuing at a rapid pace. The development threatens recent diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over alleged safety failures
cards.teaser: Florida filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of failing to warn users that ChatGPT could be dangerous while marketing it as safe.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company failed to adequately warn users about ChatGPT's dangers. The complaint accuses OpenAI of marketing the chatbot as safe and reliable while knowing it could facilitate harmful activities.

The lawsuit references a shooting at Florida State University and claims OpenAI allowed ChatGPT to aid violent incidents. Uthmeier alleges the company built a "web of deceit" around the chatbot's capabilities. This represents one of the first state-level legal challenges to an AI company over product safety concerns.

cards.headline: AI company Anthropic files for initial public offering
cards.teaser: Anthropic submitted preliminary paperwork to sell stock to the public in what could become one of the largest IPOs in US history.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced it has confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The company, which develops the Claude chatbot used by software engineers and business clients, has experienced rapid growth this year. In its most recent funding round, Anthropic raised $65 billion, valuing the company at $965 billion—a significant jump from its $380 billion valuation in February.

The Anthropic IPO is expected to rank among the largest in US history. The offering comes as other AI firms, including OpenAI and SpaceX, also prepare to go public, reflecting surging investor interest in artificial intelligence technology.

cards.headline: Killer sentenced for murder of Southampton university student
cards.teaser: A weapons-obsessed individual was jailed for killing Henry Nowak, a university student walking home from a night out.
cards.body:
A court sentenced a killer described as weapons-obsessed for the murder of Henry Nowak, a university student in Southampton, England. Nowak was killed as he walked back from a night out in the city.

The convicted individual's fascination with weapons played a role in the case, though specific details about the weapon used and the circumstances of the attack were not provided in available reports. The sentencing brings closure to a case that shocked the university community and raised concerns about student safety in the area.

cards.headline: Anthropic Files for Public Stock Offering
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company behind Claude chatbot submitted preliminary paperwork for an initial public offering that could value the company near $1 trillion.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, has filed confidential paperwork for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The company announced the filing on Monday as it prepares to offer shares to the public this year.

The announcement follows Anthropic's Series H funding round, which raised $65 billion and valued the company at $965 billion. This represents significant growth from February, when the company was valued at $380 billion. The potential IPO could rank among the largest technology offerings in US history, as Anthropic competes with other major AI firms also planning public debuts.

cards.headline: Florida Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Concerns
cards.teaser: Florida's attorney general filed a lawsuit alleging OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman concealed serious risks after multiple murders were linked to ChatGPT use.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has sued OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging the company misrepresented ChatGPT's safety to the public. The lawsuit claims OpenAI failed to warn users about potential dangers while marketing the chatbot as safe and reliable.

The case centers on violent incidents linked to ChatGPT, including a shooting at Florida State University. Uthmeier contends that OpenAI concealed serious risks associated with its technology and that the service poses particular dangers to children.

cards.headline: HPE Stock Surges 30% on Strongest Earnings Beat Since 2018
cards.teaser: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported second quarter results that exceeded expectations, driven by surging demand for AI servers.
cards.body:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares jumped 30 percent after the company reported its largest earnings beat since 2018. The technology company raised its long-term financial targets, citing strong growth projections over the next 18 months fueled by server demand.

The company said surging demand for AI computing infrastructure boosted revenue and prompted management to pull forward previously announced long-term goals. HPE has positioned itself as a beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, selling hardware that companies use to power AI applications and data processing.

cards.headline: FedEx Freight Begins Trading as Standalone Company
cards.teaser: FedEx completed the spinoff of its freight division, which began trading independently on the New York Stock Exchange.
cards.body:
FedEx Freight started trading as a separate company after FedEx completed splitting off the less-than-truckload shipping unit. Shares fell in initial trading following the market debut. The freight unit's CEO said self-driving trucks are ready for widespread commercial use.

The spinoff allows the freight business to operate independently from FedEx's package delivery operations. Analysts said the separation prompts a fresh evaluation of valuations for both the freight carrier and the remaining FedEx corporation.

cards.headline: Energy Department Limits Appliance Rebate Eligibility
cards.teaser: New guidance from the Energy Department would prevent people from receiving rebates after swapping appliances under inflation reduction programs.
cards.body:
The Energy Department issued new guidance that could phase out rebates for certain appliance swaps made under Inflation Reduction Act programs. The rules would prevent consumers from receiving rebates after making such exchanges.

The change affects homeowners who planned to take advantage of federal incentives for upgrading to more energy-efficient appliances. The rebate programs were designed to encourage Americans to replace older appliances with models that use less electricity.

cards.headline: McDonald's Plans Menu and Restaurant Changes to Attract Customers
cards.teaser: McDonald's unveiled a new global growth strategy that includes adding chicken wings to menus and remodeling restaurants to create a more upscale feel.
cards.body:
McDonald's announced a new corporate strategy focused on restaurant improvements and menu innovation as competition in the fast food industry intensifies. The company plans to add chicken wings to menus and remodel locations to appeal to diners seeking a different experience.

The changes aim to make restaurants easier to operate while attracting customers in an increasingly competitive market. The chicken wings represent McDonald's entry into a category where rivals have found success, intensifying the fast-food chicken competition.

hero.headline: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over violent incidents allegedly linked to ChatGPT
hero.body:
Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman in what appears to be the first state-level legal action of its kind against the artificial intelligence company. The lawsuit centers on violent incidents allegedly connected to ChatGPT, including a shooting at Florida State University last year.

According to Florida's Attorney General, the lawsuit accuses OpenAI of failing to warn users that ChatGPT could be dangerous. Instead, the company allegedly marketed the chatbot as safe and reliable. The complaint characterizes Altman as having an "utter disregard" for human lives.

The legal filing cites multiple violent incidents in connection with the chatbot, though the Florida State University shooting appears to be a central focus. The specific nature of ChatGPT's alleged role in these incidents has not been fully detailed in available reporting.

This lawsuit represents a significant moment in the growing legal challenges facing AI companies as their technologies become increasingly integrated into daily life. OpenAI has previously emphasized its commitment to building safety measures into ChatGPT and preventing misuse of the platform. The Florida action, however, suggests that state authorities believe these safeguards have proven inadequate in preventing real-world harm.

The legal action arrives as policymakers and regulators at both state and federal levels continue to grapple with how to address potential risks from increasingly capable AI systems. Florida's decision to pursue legal action rather than wait for new regulations represents a potentially significant shift in how states may approach AI governance.

The outcome of this case could establish important precedents for holding AI companies accountable for incidents involving their products. If Florida successfully establishes legal liability for OpenAI, it could prompt similar lawsuits in other states and potentially influence how AI companies design and deploy their systems going forward.

The decision to name Altman personally in the lawsuit is relatively uncommon and signals the severity with which Florida is treating the allegations. This approach places the CEO himself in legal jeopardy alongside the company.

As AI technology continues to advance rapidly and become embedded in consumer products and services, questions about corporate responsibility and government oversight have intensified. The Florida lawsuit illustrates how states are willing to take direct legal action to address what they view as inadequate safety protocols and transparency from major AI developers.

The case will likely attract significant attention from technology companies, regulators, and legal observers interested in understanding how courts will approach liability for AI-related harms. The outcome could reshape how AI developers market their products and what safety responsibilities they face under state law.

cards.headline: Hackers hijack Instagram accounts by exploiting Meta AI support chatbot
cards.teaser: Instagram users reported widespread account hacks after attackers tricked Meta's AI support system into granting unauthorized access.
cards.body:
Multiple Instagram users reported having their accounts hacked over the weekend after hackers exploited Meta's AI support chatbot. According to a video shared on Telegram, attackers manipulated the chatbot into changing the email address associated with victim accounts and resetting passwords, granting them full access.

Meta's support chatbot, designed to help users resolve account issues, became an entry point for unauthorized access. The incident demonstrates how AI-powered customer support systems can introduce security vulnerabilities when deployed at scale without adequate safeguards against manipulation.

cards.headline: SpaceX cites water access as risk factor in IPO filing
cards.teaser: The space company warned investors that securing abundant, affordable water for data center cooling poses challenges to its operations.
cards.body:
SpaceX has flagged water access as a risk factor in its IPO filing. The company requires significant water resources to cool its data centers and has identified access to abundant, affordable water as a challenge for its operations.

The disclosure underscores how data center operations demand substantial physical resources. Cooling systems are essential to prevent equipment failures, making reliable water access a critical component of SpaceX's infrastructure needs.

cards.headline: GM cuts development time from 15 hours to one minute using AI
cards.teaser: The automaker says artificial intelligence and machine learning have dramatically accelerated its vehicle design processes.
cards.body:
General Motors has slashed development time for certain tasks from 15 hours to just one minute using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The company is applying these technologies across virtualization processes including computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, and digital twins—virtual replicas that simulate physical systems.

This acceleration allows engineers to test vehicle designs and identify performance issues before manufacturing begins, potentially compressing development timelines and reducing costs for bringing new models to production.

cards.headline: New app The Mall creates universal shopping feed across retailers
cards.teaser: The shopping platform lets users build personalized feeds of brands and track sales across thousands of online stores.
cards.body:
The Mall is a new shopping app that aggregates products from thousands of retailers into a single personalized feed. Users can follow their favorite brands and customize what they see based on their shopping preferences.

The app helps shoppers discover products and keep track of sales and product drops across multiple retailers in one place, rather than having to visit individual store websites or apps.

hero.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett from Browns in blockbuster trade
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have acquired star edge rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in a major trade deal, multiple outlets reported Monday. The Rams sent linebacker Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round draft pick, and additional draft compensation to Cleveland in exchange for the two-time Defensive Player of the Year.

Garrett, 30, is one of the league's premier pass rushers and a seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns drafted him first overall in 2017, he has accumulated 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures, and 149 tackles for loss. In 2025, he set the single-season sacks record with 23 and earned All-Pro recognition despite the team finishing 5-12 and missing the playoffs for the second consecutive year.

Garrett had requested a trade from Cleveland in 2024 after the team started that season 3-14, stating he wanted to play for a championship contender. A month later, he signed a four-year, $160 million extension that made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal includes $122.8 million in guaranteed money and an average annual salary of $40 million.

The trade comes as the Browns undergo significant changes. Kevin Stefanski was fired as head coach in January and replaced by Todd Monken, the former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator. Monken indicated last month he had not yet met face-to-face with Garrett since taking the job.

Verse, the 25-year-old heading to Cleveland, was a first-round pick by the Rams in 2024 and earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He was selected to the Pro Bowl this past season and has 12 career sacks along with 22 tackles for loss.

The Rams, who lost to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC championship game, have a history of aggressive trades. In 2021, they acquired Matthew Stafford from the Detroit Lions and won the Super Bowl in his first season with the team. Super Bowl LXI will be played at the Rams' home SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, next February.

The acquisition significantly strengthens Los Angeles' defensive line and signals the team's commitment to competing for a championship. Both organizations confirmed the trade, with Cleveland officials acknowledging the difficulty of the decision to part with their defensive cornerstone. For the Browns, the deal provides youth and draft flexibility as they begin a rebuild under new leadership.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots for draft picks
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia Eagles have agreed to send wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in exchange for two draft picks.
cards.body:
The New England Patriots have acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade that sends two draft picks to Philadelphia. The move reunites Brown with former Tennessee Titans head coach Mike Vrabel, who now leads the Patriots. The trade gives quarterback Drake Maye a premier receiving target as New England looks to upgrade its offensive weapons.

Brown, considered a superstar at his position, spent recent seasons with the Eagles after previously playing in Tennessee. The Patriots made the trade to bolster their passing attack and provide Maye with an experienced receiver. For Philadelphia, the deal marks a significant roster change as they move on from one of their top offensive players in exchange for future draft capital.

cards.headline: Serena Williams to return to competitive tennis at age 44
cards.teaser: Serena Williams will play in the women's doubles at Queen's, marking her first competitive tennis match in nearly four years.
cards.body:
Serena Williams has announced her return to professional tennis at Queen's Club next week, nearly four years after her last competition at the 2022 US Open. The 44-year-old will compete in the women's doubles draw with a wildcard entry, partnering with Victoria Mboko. Williams called the prestigious London tournament the "perfect place" for her comeback.

This marks Williams's first competitive appearance since stepping away from the sport in 2022, when she described the move as "evolving away" from tennis. Queen's serves as a traditional warmup event ahead of Wimbledon, one of the sport's most prestigious tournaments.

cards.headline: Giants sign Odell Beckham Jr. and multiple receivers
cards.teaser: The New York Giants have brought back Odell Beckham Jr. along with signing JuJu Smith-Schuster and Braxton Berrios to strengthen their receiving corps.
cards.body:
Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has returned to the New York Giants, the team where he launched his NFL career 12 years ago. The signing marks a reunion for the former All-Pro after his time with other organizations.

The Giants also bolstered their receiving room by adding JuJu Smith-Schuster and Braxton Miller, strengthening their wide receiver group ahead of the season.

cards.headline: Ben Askren to compete after recovering from double lung transplant
cards.teaser: Former MMA fighter Ben Askren will return to wrestling less than a year after receiving a life-saving double lung transplant.
cards.body:
Ben Askren will return to wrestling competition at Real American Freestyle 11 on July 18, where he'll face former UFC champion Belal Muhammad. The 40-year-old underwent a double lung transplant after suffering severe pneumonia that threatened his life. Medical clearance has allowed him to resume athletic competition following his recovery.

The matchup marks Askren's first competition since his health crisis and transplant surgery. His return to the mat represents a significant milestone in his recovery journey.

cards.headline: Matteo Berrettini reaches first Grand Slam quarterfinal in nearly four years
cards.teaser: The Italian tennis player advanced to the French Open quarterfinals, ending a lengthy drought at the Grand Slam level after struggling with injuries.
cards.body:
Berrettini reached the quarterfinals at a Grand Slam tournament for the first time in almost four years, overcoming an extended period marked by injury problems. After his victory, Berrettini said tennis is the love of his life and expressed joy at returning to the later rounds of a major championship. The result represents a significant milestone in his comeback.

The Italian's path back to Grand Slam success followed multiple setbacks that kept him from competing at his previous level. His advancement to the quarterfinals demonstrates a return to form after the injury-plagued stretch. Berrettini's performance at the French Open signals a potential revival of his career at the sport's highest level.

cards.headline: Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska advances to French Open quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Chwalinska continued her breakthrough Grand Slam debut by defeating French player Diane Parry
cards.body:
Maja Chwalinska's remarkable French Open debut continued as the Polish qualifier defeated French player Diane Parry to reach the quarter-finals.

Chwalinska has emerged as one of the tournament's surprise stories, progressing through qualifying rounds before her unexpected run in the main draw. Her victory over Parry marks another impressive milestone in what has been described as a dream campaign for the relatively unknown player at one of tennis's biggest stages.

hero.headline: CBS Names Nick Bilton to Lead 60 Minutes After Spate of Firings
hero.body:
CBS News has appointed Nick Bilton, a former New York Times technology journalist and documentary filmmaker, as executive producer of 60 Minutes for its upcoming 59th season. The announcement comes after a significant staff shake-up at the newsmagazine under the direction of Bari Weiss, the CBS News editor in chief.

The personnel changes announced Thursday were substantial. Tanya Simon, who served as the show's top producer, was ousted from her role. Simon had taken the position after longtime executive producer Bill Owens resigned in spring 2025. The network also parted ways with correspondent Cecilia Vega, who joined the program in 2023, and Draggan Mihailovich, the executive editor. Additionally, veteran correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi was terminated after her contract was not renewed.

Both Vega and Alfonsi issued statements suggesting editorial concerns influenced their departures. Vega stated that she and her producing teams had experienced attempts to insert political bias into stories. She described the situation as "censorship, both imposed and self-driven," and said reporting teams had withheld story pitches out of fear of internal consequences. Alfonsi claimed she was penalized for pushing back on Weiss's criticisms of her December 2025 segment about a prison in El Salvador.

The changes have generated internal friction. During a staff meeting with Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, veteran correspondent Scott Pelley directly criticized CBS News management, attacking the decision to fire multiple staff members. Pelley reportedly used harsh language in condemning the leadership decisions.

Bilton brings extensive experience in technology journalism and documentary filmmaking, though he has not previously produced broadcast television programming. In a memo to staff, he acknowledged the show's historical significance while suggesting the need for evolution. "The world we are reporting on, and the world we are reporting to, where people consume their news, has moved," he wrote. "And if we don't move with it, in the ways that matter, we won't be here for the next sixty years."

He outlined his philosophy as balancing preservation with change. "I'm here to lead this show, not preserve it under glass," Bilton wrote. "That means honoring what works and being honest about what doesn't."

Weiss expressed confidence in the appointment, calling Bilton "one of the most entrepreneurial and ambitious journalists working today." However, Bilton's lack of broadcast television experience, combined with Weiss's background in opinion commentary rather than television news, has raised questions among 60 Minutes staff who had viewed Simon's promotion as an indication that CBS leadership wanted to preserve the show's established approach.

The newsmagazine has maintained its position as the most-watched news program on television for 52 consecutive seasons, averaging 9.1 million viewers in its most recent season.

cards.headline: Michael Arden Directs Stage Adaptation of The Lost Boys
cards.teaser: The Tony-winning director behind last year's best musical takes on the 1987 vampire film for the stage.
cards.body:
Michael Arden is directing The Lost Boys, a stage adaptation of the 1987 cult horror film. The production has received 12 Tony nominations, including two for Arden himself. Last year, Arden won a Tony Award for best musical with a show about two robots.

The stage version represents a major investment for producers betting on the enduring appeal of the vampire story. Arden has also announced plans for a Broadway musical adaptation of Happy Feet featuring anthropomorphic animals, though no production timeline has been set for that project.

cards.headline: Gracie Abrams Announces Third Album Daughter From Hell
cards.teaser: The singer-songwriter will release her new studio album in July, calling it her favorite music she has ever made.
cards.body:
Gracie Abrams will release her third studio album, Daughter From Hell, on July 17. The singer-songwriter described the upcoming record as her favorite music she has ever made. The announcement follows two previous studio albums that established her in the contemporary pop landscape.

Abrams has built a following through introspective songwriting and collaborations with other artists. The July release date positions the album for summer touring season and festival appearances.

cards.headline: Outlander: Blood of My Blood Returns to Starz in September
cards.teaser: The prequel series will launch its second season in mid-September with a first teaser released.
cards.body:
Outlander: Blood of My Blood Season 2 will premiere on Starz on Sept. 18. The network released the first teaser for the romantic epic prequel series, which continues the stories introduced in the first season. The show explores the backstories of characters Claire and Jamie from the original Outlander series.

The prequel format allows the franchise to expand its timeline while maintaining connections to the main series. Starz has invested in the Outlander universe as a cornerstone of its scripted programming lineup.

cards.headline: Bad Bunny Wraps Global Tour With Surprise Performances
cards.teaser: The Puerto Rican star played surprise hits and ended yearslong rivalries onstage during recent shows.
cards.body:
Bad Bunny has been delivering notable moments during his current global tour, including surprise song selections and onstage reconciliations. The Puerto Rican artist ended yearslong rivalries during performances, though specific details about which artists were involved were not provided in reports. He also performed unexpected songs from his catalog.

The tour has taken Bad Bunny to venues worldwide as he promotes his latest music. Concert highlights have generated significant attention on social media and among music fans following the tour stops.

cards.headline: Antoni Porowski Discusses Post-Queer Eye Career Transition
cards.teaser: The television personality addresses drama from the show and his new travel series Best of the World.
cards.body:
After nearly a decade on Queer Eye, Antoni Porowski is navigating a new chapter in his career. His first project following the show is Best of the World, a travel series that takes him to Mexico City, London, Paris, and New York City.

Porowski has described himself as thriving on uncertainty and views his current period as a transition. He addressed drama related to Queer Eye and explored finding LGBTQ+ community through his travel work. Despite these developments, Porowski says he still has more questions than answers about where his career will lead next.

cards.headline: Love Island U.K. Returns for 13th Season
cards.teaser: The original Love Island series launches with a new cast at the Majorca villa, available for U.S. viewers.
cards.body:
Love Island U.K. Season 13 begins with a new group of singles at the show's Majorca villa location. The reality dating series returns for its 13th season, maintaining the format that established it as a cultural phenomenon in Britain and internationally.

U.S. audiences can access the show through streaming platforms, though specific viewing instructions vary by service. The U.K. version predates the American adaptation and continues to draw substantial viewership across multiple territories.

hero.headline: Maine Governor Mills reminds voters she remains in Senate primary race
hero.teaser: Mills clarified she suspended but did not drop her campaign as voters weigh allegations against frontrunner Graham Platner.
hero.body:
Maine Governor Janet Mills clarified her status in the Democratic Senate primary race on Monday, saying voters have the mistaken impression that she withdrew or dropped out of the contest.

Mills suspended her active campaign for the U.S. Senate in recent weeks, citing a lack of financial resources to compete effectively. However, she did not formally remove her name from the ballot. The clarification comes as Democratic voters consider the implications of recent reports involving her main rival in the primary.

Graham Platner, a first-time candidate and oyster farmer who previously served in the Marine Corps, has emerged as the frontrunner in the Democratic race. The primary will determine which Democrat faces Republican incumbent Susan Collins in what has become one of the most closely watched Senate competitions in the country.

When Mills announced her decision to suspend her campaign, she explained that while she possessed the drive, passion, commitment, experience and willingness to fight, she lacked the necessary financial resources that modern political campaigns require. Despite her departure from active campaigning, she left open the possibility of supporting the eventual Democratic nominee.

Mills had initially entered the race with strong backing from the Democratic establishment. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee chair Kirsten Gillibrand had supported her candidacy as Democrats sought to gain seats and reclaim control of the Senate.

Throughout the primary contest, Mills struggled to compete with Platner, who drew large crowds to campaign events across Maine. Platner led by double digits in recent polling and secured endorsements from prominent national senators including Elizabeth Warren, Bernie Sanders and Chris Van Hollen.

Mills attempted to highlight controversies from Platner's past during the campaign. She aired advertisements featuring women responding to a 2013 Reddit post in which Platner suggested that sexual assault survivors and victims should take responsibility and avoid getting intoxicated. Platner has since called those comments inexcusable while attributing them partly to trauma from his military service.

Additional scrutiny of Platner's background surfaced over the past year, including unearthed racist, sexist and homophobic online comments and a tattoo resembling a Nazi symbol that he later covered.

Despite these controversies, Platner maintained support among Maine voters who are drawn to his anti-establishment message. He has argued that his past statements have already been thoroughly discussed and addressed since October of the previous year.

With Mills no longer actively campaigning, Platner stands as the presumptive Democratic nominee heading into the general election against Collins. The race will test whether Maine voters will reject the Trump administration and current Republican leadership in the upcoming midterm elections.

cards.headline: Trump administration scraps $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund after Republican pushback
cards.teaser: The Trump administration abandoned its nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund following criticism from congressional Republicans and a court challenge ques.
cards.body:
The Trump administration abandoned a $1.8 billion fund created from an IRS settlement after facing opposition from Republican lawmakers and a legal challenge. Republican Representative Kat Cammack criticized the fund as a "billion-dollar-plus slush fund," arguing it wasn't an appropriate solution to government weaponization concerns. The administration dismantled the fund later that same day.

The fund drew immediate scrutiny from within Trump's own party, with more than a dozen Republican senators urging the administration to reverse course. Critics characterized it as a scheme favoring political allies while lacking transparency and oversight. A federal judge in Florida reopened the underlying IRS case, adding legal pressure to the controversial initiative.

cards.headline: Senate candidate Platner to meet with Democratic senators in Washington
cards.teaser: The Maine Democratic primary frontrunner will face questions from senators about sexting allegations reported by major newspapers.
cards.body:
Maine Democratic Senate primary candidate Graham Platner is scheduled to meet with Democratic senators in Washington on Tuesday afternoon. The long-planned meeting will give senators an opportunity to ask Platner directly about the allegations.

The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times reported that Platner sent sexually explicit text messages to as many as a dozen women in 2023. Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey indicated over the weekend that he had questions about the allegations. Platner also has fundraisers scheduled during his Washington visit.

cards.headline: National Republican Senatorial Committee establishes joint fundraising with Texas Attorney General Paxton
cards.teaser: The committee now partners with Paxton after spending months attacking him during his primary challenge.
cards.body:
The National Republican Senatorial Committee has joined with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton to create a joint fundraising committee. The arrangement comes after the committee spent months attacking Paxton during his primary race against Senator John Cornyn.

Paxton won the primary last week, defeating the incumbent Cornyn. The NRSC's decision to partner with Paxton represents a shift from its earlier opposition to his candidacy during the Republican primary contest.

cards.headline: Iowa Democrats dispute characterization of party ahead of Senate primary
cards.teaser: The state party faces competitive races for Senate, House seats, and the governor's office ahead of Tuesday's primary.
cards.body:
Iowa Democrats rejected suggestions that their party is in disarray as they prepare to select a Senate nominee on Tuesday. The state faces a competitive Senate race along with surprisingly competitive elections for House seats and the governor's office in November.

The Tuesday primary will determine which Democrat will compete in what party officials describe as a competitive Senate contest. Iowa also has multiple House races that Democrats view as potentially winnable in the fall elections.

cards.headline: Carnival data breach affects nearly 6 million cruise passengers
cards.teaser: The cruise company disclosed an April breach that exposed personal information of travelers.
cards.body:
Carnival cruise line reported a data breach in April that exposed personal information of nearly 6 million passengers. The company advised affected travelers to take steps to safeguard their personal information.

Carnival disclosed the breach publicly, acknowledging that passenger data had been compromised. The company has not specified what types of personal information were accessed in the breach.

cards.headline: Southwest Airlines modifies plus-size seating policy months after implementation
cards.teaser: The airline walked back a key part of its new guidelines for plus-size travelers.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines changed its seating guidelines for plus-size travelers, reversing a key part of a policy implemented just months earlier. An advocacy group said the modifications do not go far enough.

The airline had recently introduced new seating policies affecting how plus-size passengers are accommodated on flights. Southwest has now rolled back at least one significant element of those guidelines, though advocacy groups remain dissatisfied with the revised policy.
